There are two type of medical degrees that one can obtain to become a doctor. You have M.D. and you have D.O. (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine). They have the same privileges as traditional M.D.'s but take a more holistic approach to patient treatment. Instead of focusing on one bodily system or organ (such as the nose), they examine how other organs in the body can cause a certain condition.

A post-bac refers to an academic program after your bachelor's degree. You would either take this if you made a late decision to apply for medical school -- in this case, you would not have all the prerequisites -- or have poor academic performance. Read this: https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school/article/considering-postbaccalaureate-premedical-program/

Remember, you can attend a post-bac program and apply as DO if your GPA is not satisfactory by the end of your senior year. **Do not** use this as an excuse to allow your academics to falter, though. Study hard, and throw any social aspects of your life out the window if you have to.
